name: Mahogany Red
lede: Mahogany Red is a warm red-brown named for the hardwood, and Maerz and Paul's dictionary dates it to 1843.

sections.title: Another mahogany
sections.body:
St Clair defines mahogany as a red brown, after the hardwood [1]. This swatch is Ridgway's, from plate II, hue 7, tone k of his 1912 atlas, and it is also in ISCC-NBS block 43 [2]. Maerz and Paul's dictionary records the name as first used in 1843, half a century earlier than the 1892 it gives for [[mahogany-brown]] [2]. The plain wood color is [[mahogany]].

The two mahoganies are separate swatches. Mahogany Red is the lighter and redder one, close to [[brick]] in family and only a little brighter than [[burnt-umber]] [2]. Our library also pairs it with the Japanese name Sencha-iro, "green tea-colored", as a secondary name [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 1,880 (7.9 per cent) hold a color within six units of this swatch over at least five per cent of the canvas [3]. It peaks in the 1400s, with 167 of 945 works, 2.2 times the archive rate [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [3]. Ridgway's plate is itself a scan of an aged page, so the swatch is approximate [2].

origin.source: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour; ColorHub library
